faqs.q: What are the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves used for?
faqs.a: Anfield needle valves and flow control valves throttle hydraulic flow through a variable orifice, in NPT sizes from 1/4" to 1" and SAE O-ring boss ports. The listing carries 20 part numbers, all rated 5,000 psi.

faqs.q: Which sizes are the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves available in?
faqs.a: The listing carries 20 part numbers: flow control needle valves such as NFC1/2NPT and NFCSAE6, and plain needle valves such as NNV1NPT. Ports are NPT from 1/4" to 1" and ORB (SAE) from #4 to #16, so pick the part number by port thread and size.

faqs.q: How should I select the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves for my application?
faqs.a: Choose the port size and thread first, then decide between a flow control needle valve (NFC) and a plain needle valve (NNV), as the item names list them. Every part number is rated 5,000 psi, so size on flow and port rather than pressure.

faqs.q: What working pressure applies to the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves?
faqs.a: Every part number in the Anfield listing is rated 5,000 psi, as shown on each row. Use the rating as the cold working pressure and check the temperature limits with us for hot service.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves offered in?
faqs.a: The listing does not state the body or seal material for the Anfield needle valves, so we confirm it from the maker when you enquire. Tell us the fluid and temperature and we check the seals against them.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves?
faqs.a: The listing names no ISO or ASME standard for the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves and holds no certificates. If your project needs a material or conformity certificate, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can issue. See [our guide to mobile hydraulic control valves](/blog/mobile-hydraulic-control-valves-guide) for how the valve types differ.

faqs.q: Which parts do the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves mate with?
faqs.a: The Anfield needle valves and flow control valves sit in the line between the pump or valve and the actuator, with ports that take matching NPT, SAE or BSPP fittings. Check the port thread and size against your hose and fittings before ordering.

faqs.q: How do I fit and look after the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves?
faqs.a: Fit the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves with flow in the direction marked on the body, set the knob slowly with the pump running and lock the setting once the actuator speed is right. A needle valve throttles by changing an orifice, so actuator speed still varies with load unless a pressure-compensated control is used instead.

faqs.q: Where are the Anfield needle valves and flow control valves used?
faqs.a: The Anfield needle valves and flow control valves are used to set the speed of cylinders and motors, to damp pressure surges and to isolate or meter flow to gauges and test points in hydraulic circuits.

faqs.a: The Anfield valves are all rated 5,000 psi with NPT and SAE ports in 20 part numbers, while [the Dynamic Fluid Components JP needle and flow control valves](/p/dynamic-fluid-components-jp-needle-and-flow-control-valves) carry 16 part numbers with NPT and SAE ports and include both needle and flow control valves. Choose on port code and stock of the exact part number.
